analysis:
Reviewed all five primary analyses and independently checked the supplied replayed patches, metadata and changelog. MediaIngest.swift head:773–776 adds two exact base64 video-label aliases; head:798 preserves case-insensitive allowlist matching and head:803 retains the decoded-byte-limit argument. This does not visibly admit external URLs, create plaintext files or remove a resource limit. No concrete regression is supported by this provider change.
Cross-file documentation in docs/architecture/inference.md head:810–815 and changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md:3 describes accepting VFR tracks using presentation-order indices and nominalFrameRate. The inference patch retains the decoded-frame cap, prepared-pixel cap, media prefix-cache exclusion and target-only decoding. Head:1896–1899 documents byte-based container identification for the expanded labels. These claims are consistent but do not prove implementation enforcement. No supplied executable change establishes altered authorization, attestation, hop encryption, billing, token custody or privileged-helper authority.
Material uncertainty remains: libs/mlx-swift-lm head:1 changes the dependency revision without its implementation delta. Review that delta, especially GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset and its budget callers, for finite positive frame rates, bounded scan/decode work, cancellation and conservative reservations under adversarial VFR timestamps. Verify MemoryBackedVideoAsset still enforces MP4/QuickTime sniffing, external-reference restrictions, memory-backed custody and resource limits for both aliases (A-001, TB-007, T-050, T-010). Check any other dependency changes against T-007, T-028 and T-041. The threat-model update reported by unit 4 could not be directly rechecked because replay is incomplete (10 omitted units). Missing implementation and replay are coverage limits, not observed missing controls; deeper review is required before clearing the dependency change.
